title: Common zero stabilization of finite free generating surjections
statement:
Let $R$ be a commutative ring, let $M$ be an $R$-module, let $n,m\ge0$, and put $F=R^{\oplus n}$ and $G=R^{\oplus m}$ [def-weil-pbc-free-module]. Let $\pi:F\twoheadrightarrow M$ and $\pi':G\twoheadrightarrow M$ be surjective $R$-linear maps. There exist $R$-linear maps $f:G\to F$ and $g:F\to G$ such that $\pi f=\pi'$ and $\pi'g=\pi$. For any such $f,g$, the map
$$U:F\oplus G\longrightarrow G\oplus F,\qquad U(x,y)=(y+g(x-fy),x-fy)$$
is an $R$-linear isomorphism with inverse
$$U^{-1}(a,b)=(b+f(a-gb),a-gb).$$
Writing $p(x,y)=\pi(x)$ and $q(a,b)=\pi'(a)$, one has $q\circ U=p$ and $U(\ker\pi\oplus G)=\ker\pi'\oplus F$.

proof.text: By [def-weil-pbc-free-module], the standard bases make $F$ and $G$ free. By [lem-weil-pbc-free-module-projective] both are projective. Apply the lifting-along-surjections characterization in [def-weil-pbc-projective-module] first with projective domain $G$, surjection $\pi:F\twoheadrightarrow M$, and map $\pi\prime:G\to M$, obtaining $f:G\to F$ with $\pi f=\pi\prime$. Apply it again with projective domain $F$, surjection $\pi\prime$, and map $\pi$, obtaining $g:F\to G$ with $\pi\prime g=\pi$.

source.place: Tag 05CE (definition-projective), following paragraph: surjectivity of Hom along surjections; Tag 05CF (lemma-characterize-projective), proof of (2) implies (1): free modules are projective

proof.text: Fix any such $f,g$. Define $V(a,b)=(b+f(a-gb),a-gb)$. Each coordinate of $U$ and $V$ is a sum or difference of composites of linear maps and coordinate projections, so both preserve addition and scalar multiplication. To check $VU=1$, put $b=x-fy$ and $a=y+gb$. Then $a-gb=y$ and $b+f(a-gb)=x-fy+fy=x$. Conversely, for arbitrary $(a,b)$ put $y=a-gb$ and $x=b+fy$. Then $x-fy=b$ and $y+g(x-fy)=a-gb+gb=a$, so $UV=1$. Thus $U$ is a linear isomorphism with inverse $V$, exactly as displayed in the statement.

proof.text: For all $(x,y)$, linearity and the two lift equations give $qU(x,y)=\pi\prime(y+g(x-fy))=\pi\prime y+\pi(x-fy)=\pi\prime y+\pi x-\pi fy=\pi x=p(x,y)$. Therefore $q\circ U=p$.

proof.text: By definition, $\ker p=\ker\pi\oplus G$ and $\ker q=\ker\pi\prime\oplus F$: membership on either side says that the first coordinate maps to zero. If $z\in\ker p$, then $q(Uz)=p(z)=0$, so $Uz\in\ker q$. Conversely, for $w\in\ker q$ take $z=Vw$. The inverse equations and $qU=p$ give $p(z)=q(UVw)=q(w)=0$, and $Uz=UVw=w$. This proves both inclusions $U(\ker\pi\oplus G)=\ker\pi\prime\oplus F$.

lean.statement: theorem free_surjections_common_stabilization (R : Type u) [CommRing R] (M : Type v) [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] (n m : ℕ) (π : (Fin n → R) →ₗ[R] M) (π' : (Fin m → R) →ₗ[R] M) (hπ : Function.Surjective π) (hπ' : Function.Surjective π') : (∃ (f : (Fin m → R) →ₗ[R] (Fin n → R)) (g : (Fin n → R) →ₗ[R] (Fin m → R)), π.comp f = π' ∧ π'.comp g = π) ∧ (∀ (f : (Fin m → R) →ₗ[R] (Fin n → R)) (g : (Fin n → R) →ₗ[R] (Fin m → R)), π.comp f = π' → π'.comp g = π → ∃ U : ((Fin n → R) × (Fin m → R)) ≃ₗ[R] ((Fin m → R) × (Fin n → R)), (∀ (x : Fin n → R) (y : Fin m → R), U (x, y) = (y + g (x - f y), x - f y)) ∧ (∀ (a : Fin m → R) (b : Fin n → R), U.symm (a, b) = (b + f (a - g b), a - g b)) ∧ (π'.comp (LinearMap.fst R (Fin m → R) (Fin n → R))).comp U.toLinearMap = π.comp (LinearMap.fst R (Fin n → R) (Fin m → R)) ∧ Submodule.map U.toLinearMap ((LinearMap.ker π).prod ⊤) = (LinearMap.ker π').prod ⊤)
